title: Specialists, merged: what task arithmetic keeps of six specialists
purpose: Train one specialist per family from the same base, merge their weights in one model with trimming and sign agreement (TIES) and with plain averaged task vectors, and score the merged models against the specialists, the generalist and the base.

checks.description: all six specialists, both merges and both evaluations completed
checks.because: Six training runs, then two merge jobs that read the specialists' weights from the bucket, then two evaluation jobs that read the merged weights back.

checks.description: each specialist improves its own family: at least four of six by 0.05 or more
checks.because: A specialist trains on one family only for 40 steps; its own family is what its reward measures.

checks.description: the merged models are complete models: every tensor of the base is present (310 of 310) and they score above zero on every family
checks.because: The merge reads six checkpoints and the base, writes one safetensors file and the base's configuration files, and the evaluation loads it into vLLM like any other model.

checks.description: merging keeps part of what the specialists learned: the TIES-merged model keeps a positive share of the gain in at least half of the families whose specialist gained
checks.because: A task vector is the specialist's weights minus the base; trimming keeps the largest 20% of each and sign agreement drops the coordinates the specialists disagree on. What survives is added to the base.

notes: Gain kept (mean over the families where a specialist gained): TIES 0.94, task arithmetic 0.68. Mean effect of the other five specialists on a family (the merged model's raw material): math +0.009, code +0.003, instr -0.010, tools +0.011, multiling +0.012, safety +0.008. Merged mean 0.764 (TIES) and 0.705 (arithmetic); generalist 0.794. Compute: six specialists at 40 steps each is twice the generalist's 120 steps.
